title: Las cosas
goal: Name everyday things with the right 'the' and 'a', in the singular and the plural.

lessons.title: The and a
lessons.notes:
Every Spanish noun is masculine or feminine - it's grammar, not meaning (a table isn't female!). The little words in front show which:
**el** libro (the book) · **un** libro (a book) - masculine
**la** mesa (the table) · **una** mesa (a table) - feminine
A good first clue: nouns ending in **-o** are usually masculine, in **-a** usually feminine. Always learn a noun together with its el or la, as one chunk.
**Un / una** also means 'one': **un libro** is 'a book' or 'one book'.

items.note: Mexico often says la pluma; Spain says el boli.
Ends in -e: just learn it with la.

It's a table.

lessons.title: Tricky genders
lessons.notes:
The -o / -a rule has famous exceptions:
**la mano** (the hand) is feminine - an old Latin word that kept its gender.
**el día** (the day) and **el mapa** are masculine despite the -a.
Words ending in **-ma** from Greek are masculine: **el problema**, **el programa**.
**La foto** is short for la fotografía, so it stays feminine.
Other endings give clues: **-ción** and **-dad** are feminine (**la televisión**, **la ciudad**); most other consonants lean masculine (**el hotel**). **-e** can go either way (**el café**, **la noche**, **la calle**): learn it with its article.

lessons.title: Plurals
lessons.notes:
To make a plural:
Ending in a vowel: add **-s** - libro → **libros**, mesa → **mesas**, café → **cafés**.
Ending in a consonant: add **-es** - hotel → **hoteles**, ciudad → **ciudades**.
A final **z** becomes **c**: el lápiz → **los lápices**.
The little words change too: el → **los**, la → **las**, un → **unos**, una → **unas** (unos / unas = some).
A group of mixed genders is masculine: **los niños** can be boys, or boys and girls.

lessons.title: Everyday things
lessons.notes:
**¿Qué es esto?** (what's this?) is the most useful question for building vocabulary - point and ask.
**El agua** (water) is feminine but takes **el**: a feminine word starting with a stressed 'a' sound uses el in the singular, just to avoid 'la agua' running together. It's still feminine: **el agua fría**, and **las aguas** in the plural.
Regional words: Latin America says **la computadora**, Spain **el ordenador**; glasses are **los lentes** in much of Latin America and **las gafas** in Spain. Some things are plural in Spanish just as in English: **los lentes**.

items.note: Feminine, but 'el agua' in the singular.
